raw: Act 4, Scene 2 — Hall in Capulet’s House
Enter Capulet, Lady Capulet, Nurse and Servants.

sentences.en: Capulet, Lady Capulet, the Nurse, and Servants enter.

speaker: CAPULET
raw: So many guests invite as here are writ.

sentences.en: Invite as many guests as are written here.

raw: Exit first Servant.

speaker: CAPULET
raw: Sirrah, go hire me twenty cunning cooks.

sentences.en: You there, go hire twenty skilled cooks for me.

speaker: SECOND SERVANT
raw:
You shall have none ill, sir; for I’ll try if they can lick their
fingers.

sentences.en: You will not have any bad ones, sir.
I will check if they can lick their fingers.

speaker: CAPULET
raw: How canst thou try them so?

sentences.en: How can you test them like that?

speaker: SECOND SERVANT
raw:
Marry, sir, ’tis an ill cook that cannot lick his own fingers;
therefore he that cannot lick his fingers goes not with me.

sentences.en: Well, sir, it is a bad cook who cannot lick his own fingers.
Therefore, anyone who cannot lick their fingers will not come with me.

speaker: CAPULET
raw: Go, begone.

sentences.en: Go away.

raw: Exit second Servant.

speaker: CAPULET
raw:
We shall be much unfurnish’d for this time.
What, is my daughter gone to Friar Lawrence?

sentences.en: We will be very short of staff for this event.
Has my daughter gone to Friar Lawrence?

speaker: NURSE
raw: Ay, forsooth.

sentences.en: Yes, truly.

speaker: CAPULET
raw:
Well, he may chance to do some good on her.
A peevish self-will’d harlotry it is.

sentences.en: Well, he might do her some good.
She is a stubborn, spoiled, selfish girl.

raw: Enter Juliet.

speaker: NURSE
raw: See where she comes from shrift with merry look.

sentences.en: Look, she is coming from confession with a happy look.

speaker: CAPULET
raw: How now, my headstrong. Where have you been gadding?

sentences.en: Well, my stubborn girl!
Where have you been running around?

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Where I have learnt me to repent the sin
Of disobedient opposition
To you and your behests; and am enjoin’d
By holy Lawrence to fall prostrate here,
To beg your pardon. Pardon, I beseech you.
Henceforward I am ever rul’d by you.

sentences.en: I have learned to repent for my sin.
I disobeyed you and your orders.
Holy Lawrence told me to fall here before you.
I am asking for your pardon.
Please forgive me.
From now on, I will always obey you.

speaker: CAPULET
raw:
Send for the County, go tell him of this.
I’ll have this knot knit up tomorrow morning.

sentences.en: Send for the Count and tell him about this.
I will have this wedding knot tied tomorrow morning.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
I met the youthful lord at Lawrence’ cell,
And gave him what becomed love I might,
Not stepping o’er the bounds of modesty.

sentences.en: I met the young lord at Lawrence's cell.
I showed him love in a proper way.
I did not go beyond the limits of modesty.

speaker: CAPULET
raw:
Why, I am glad on’t. This is well. Stand up.
This is as’t should be. Let me see the County.
Ay, marry. Go, I say, and fetch him hither.
Now afore God, this reverend holy Friar,
All our whole city is much bound to him.

sentences.en: I am glad about this.
This is good.
Stand up.
This is how it should be.
Let me see the Count.
Yes, yes.
Go and fetch him here.
Before God, our whole city owes much to this holy Friar.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Nurse, will you go with me into my closet,
To help me sort such needful ornaments
As you think fit to furnish me tomorrow?

sentences.en: Nurse, will you go into my room with me?
You can help me choose the necessary jewelry.
Choose the items that you think are right for me to wear tomorrow.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw: No, not till Thursday. There is time enough.

sentences.en: No, not until Thursday.
There is enough time.

speaker: CAPULET
raw: Go, Nurse, go with her. We’ll to church tomorrow.

sentences.en: Go, Nurse, go with her.
We will go to church tomorrow.

raw: Exeunt Juliet and Nurse.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
We shall be short in our provision,
’Tis now near night.

sentences.en: We will not have enough supplies.
It is almost night.

speaker: CAPULET
raw:
Tush, I will stir about,
And all things shall be well, I warrant thee, wife.
Go thou to Juliet, help to deck up her.
I’ll not to bed tonight, let me alone.
I’ll play the housewife for this once.—What, ho!—
They are all forth: well, I will walk myself
To County Paris, to prepare him up
Against tomorrow. My heart is wondrous light
Since this same wayward girl is so reclaim’d.

sentences.en: Nonsense, I will take care of things.
Everything will be fine, I promise you, wife.
Go to Juliet and help her get dressed.
I will not go to bed tonight.
Leave me alone.
I will do the housework just this once.
They are all out.
Well, I will walk to Count Paris myself.
I will prepare him for tomorrow.
My heart is light because this stubborn girl has changed her ways.

raw: Exeunt.
